analysis:
The code snippet calls `Arrays.fill(durationsUs, oldDurationsUsCount, newDurationsUsCount, C.TIME_UNSET)`. The arguments are: array `durationsUs` (after `Arrays.copyOf` its length is `newDurationsUsCount`), `fromIndex = oldDurationsUsCount`, `toIndex = newDurationsUsCount`, `val = C.TIME_UNSET`. The API documentation declares two exceptions: `IllegalArgumentException` if `fromIndex > toIndex`, and `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` if `fromIndex < 0` or `toIndex > a.length`. 
- For `IllegalArgumentException`: `fromIndex` is `oldDurationsUsCount`, `toIndex` is `newDurationsUsCount`. Since `newDurationsUsCount = Math.max(count, oldDurationsUsCount)`, we have `newDurationsUsCount >= oldDurationsUsCount`. Thus `fromIndex <= toIndex`. Equality (range empty) is allowed, so condition avoided. 
- For `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`: `fromIndex = oldDurationsUsCount >= 0` because array lengths are non-negative. `toIndex = newDurationsUsCount` equals the array length after `copyOf`, so `toIndex == a.length`. The exception triggers only if `toIndex > a.length`, not on equality. Thus condition avoided. 
Both declared exceptions are avoided by the logic of the code.
remark: Both exceptions are fully avoided in this context. The code ensures `fromIndex <= toIndex` and `toIndex` exactly equals the array length, with `fromIndex` non-negative. Therefore no exception from `Arrays.fill` will be thrown.
